questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: Water ____ at 0 °C.
questions.explanation: Universal truths take the simple present: *Water freezes at 0 °C.*
option_feedback: A scientific fact is always in the simple present, not the continuous.
Facts do not belong only to the past.
*Water* is singular: add -s.
Correct!

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: Listen! Someone ____ at the door.
questions.explanation: *Listen!* / *Look!* signal an action in progress: present continuous.
option_feedback: *Listen!* points to now, not the past.
The knocking is still going on as we listen.
Correct!
*Listen!* shows the action is happening right now: use the continuous.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: My father ____ his car every Sunday.
option_feedback: A regular habit is not expressed with the present perfect.
Correct!
*My father* is third person singular: *washes*.
*every Sunday* shows a habit, so the simple present is used.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: I ____ this film three times already.
questions.explanation: *already* + experience up to now → present perfect: *have seen*.
option_feedback: Correct!
*already* and *three times* (experience up to now) call for the present perfect.
After *have* use V3: *seen*, not *saw*.
*see* in this sense is not used in the continuous.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: She ____ in this school since 2018.
questions.explanation: *since 2018* + still going on → present perfect continuous.
option_feedback: *since 2018* needs a perfect tense, not the present continuous.
*since* + a point of time takes the present perfect (continuous).
She still teaches here; the simple past would mean she stopped.
Correct!

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: The Ganga ____ into the Bay of Bengal.
option_feedback: The river still flows there; it is a permanent fact.
*The Ganga* is singular: *flows*.
Correct!
A permanent geographical fact takes the simple present.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: We ____ for the bus for forty minutes, and it still hasn't come.
questions.explanation: *for* + a period up to now, still continuing → present perfect continuous.
option_feedback: The simple present does not show a period of time continuing up to now.
Correct!
*for forty minutes* (a length of time up to now) needs the perfect continuous.
*it still hasn't come* shows the waiting continues now.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: Do you ____ where Meena lives?
option_feedback: Correct!
After *do/does* we use V1 with no -s.
After *do* use V1, not V2.
After *do* use V1, not the -ing form.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: The train to Ahmedabad ____ at 6:45 tomorrow morning.
questions.explanation: Timetables take the simple present even for the future.
option_feedback: *tomorrow* is in the future.
*tomorrow* is future; the present perfect cannot refer to it.
Past perfect cannot point to tomorrow.
Correct!

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: This soup ____ delicious.
option_feedback: *taste* meaning "has a flavour" is a stative verb, so no continuous.
*This soup* is singular: *tastes*.
A stative meaning is not used in the continuous.
Correct!

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: Have you finished your homework ____?
questions.explanation: *yet* is used in questions and negatives with the present perfect.
option_feedback: *since* needs a point of time after it.
*ago* goes with the simple past, not the present perfect.
Correct!
In questions and negatives about something expected, we normally use *yet*.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: Neither of the boys ____ the answer.
option_feedback: The subject *neither* is singular, so *have* is wrong.
Correct!
*Neither of* + plural noun takes a singular verb in formal English.
*know* is stative, and the subject is singular.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: Mahatma Gandhi ____ the Dandi March in 1930.
questions.explanation: A definite past time → simple past.
option_feedback: Correct!
*in 1930* is a finished time: no present perfect.
This is a historical fact in the past.
There is no second past action to make this the earlier one.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: While I ____ my bicycle, it started to rain.
questions.explanation: *While* + longer action in progress → past continuous.
option_feedback: *While* introduces a longer action in progress: past continuous.
The riding was going on, not finished, when the rain started.
*started* shows the story is in the past.
Correct!

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: The thief ____ before the police reached the spot.
questions.explanation: Earlier of two past actions → past perfect.
option_feedback: The story is in the past (*reached*).
*before the police reached* shows the escape was complete.
Correct!
The escape happened first; to show that clearly, use the past perfect.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: She didn't ____ the bus yesterday.
option_feedback: After *didn't*, V1 with no -s.
Correct!
After *did/didn't* always use V1.
After *didn't* use V1, not V-ing.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: When I entered the hall, the chief guest ____ his speech.
questions.explanation: Action in progress at a past moment → past continuous.
option_feedback: Correct!
*entered* sets the time in the past.
The speech was in progress at that past moment.
The subject is singular and the time is past.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: They ____ for three hours when the rescue team found them.
questions.explanation: Duration up to a past moment → past perfect continuous.
option_feedback: *for three hours* before a past event needs the past perfect continuous.
The story is in the past (*found*).
The simple past does not show the duration before *found*.
Correct!

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: After he ____ his breakfast, he went to the office.
option_feedback: *After* shows the breakfast was finished first.
Both actions are in the past.
Correct!
The story is in the past (*went*).

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: The old man ____ under the tree when the storm began.
option_feedback: He was still asleep when the storm began.
The time is past (*began*).
Correct!
His sleeping was going on and the storm interrupted it.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: I ____ him a letter last month, but he hasn't replied yet.
option_feedback: *last month* needs the past.
Correct!
*last month* is a finished time.
No second past action is mentioned to need the past perfect.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: The sun ____ when we reached the hilltop, so we missed the sunset.
questions.explanation: Completed before the past moment → *had already set*.
option_feedback: Correct!
*reached* puts the story in the past.
The setting happened before we reached; the past perfect makes the order clear.
*missed the sunset* means it was completely over.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: Look at those dark clouds! It ____ rain.
questions.explanation: Prediction from present evidence → *be going to*.
option_feedback: When there is present evidence (*dark clouds*), we prefer *going to*.
The rain has not started yet.
*has rain* is not a correct form.
Correct!

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: This time next week, we ____ on the beach in Goa.
questions.explanation: In progress at a future time → future continuous.
option_feedback: This is a future time, and the action is in progress.
We will be in the middle of relaxing, not finished.
Correct!
*This time next week* points to an action in progress at a future moment.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: By the end of this year, I ____ all twelve chapters.
option_feedback: Present perfect cannot point to the end of this year.
Correct!
*By the end of this year* means completed before that time.
The time is in the future.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: If you ____ hard, you will surely pass.
option_feedback: Correct!
No *will* in an *if* clause.
The result clause *will pass* calls for the present in the *if* clause.
A general condition takes the simple present.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: Don't worry, I ____ you with your project.
option_feedback: A promise or decision made on the spot takes *will*.
The help is a future promise, not a habit.
The help is still to come.
Correct!

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: Please wait here until I ____ back.
option_feedback: The meaning is future; use the present in the time clause.
A single future event in a time clause takes the simple present.
Correct!
No *will* after *until* (a time clause).

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: By next April, my grandfather ____ in this village for sixty years.
questions.explanation: Duration up to a future point → future perfect continuous.
option_feedback: The time is future.
Correct!
*for sixty years* up to *next April* shows a duration ending at a future point.
*By next April* is a future point.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: He told me that he ____ busy.
questions.explanation: Past main verb → past in the clause.
option_feedback: Sequence of tenses: after *told*, use a past form.
Correct!
The main verb *told* is in the past, so the clause moves back: *was*.
After a past reporting verb, *will* changes to *would*.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: Our teacher said that honesty ____ the best policy.
questions.explanation: Universal truths keep the present even after a past verb.
option_feedback: Correct!
A universal truth or proverb stays in the present.
Universal truths do not change tense.
*honesty* is singular, and the truth stays present.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: I hoped that she ____ the competition.
option_feedback: After a past verb (*hoped*), *will* becomes *would*.
Sequence of tenses needs a past form.
After *hoped*, a past form is needed.
Correct!

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: She worked hard so that she ____ get a scholarship.
questions.explanation: Purpose clause after a past verb → *might/could*.
option_feedback: The main verb is past; use *could* or *might*.
*will* does not express purpose here, and the main verb is past.
Correct!
After a past verb, *may* becomes *might*.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: We knew that the earth ____ round the sun.
questions.explanation: Exception to the sequence of tenses: universal truths.
option_feedback: The fact is permanent, so the simple present.
Correct!
A scientific truth stays in the simple present.
Scientific truths do not shift into the past.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct option: He ran fast lest he ____ the train.
option_feedback: Correct!
*lest* is followed by *should* + V1.
*lest* already means *so that ... not*; a second *not* is wrong.
*lest* takes *should* + V1.

questions.question:

*Rahul ____ (a) cricket since he was six. Last year he ____ (b) selected for the district team, and next month he ____ (c) in the state trials.*

Blank (a):
questions.explanation: *since he was six* + still continuing → *has been playing*.
option_feedback: He still plays; the simple past would mean he stopped.
*since* + point of time does not go with the simple present.
Correct!
*since he was six* needs the present perfect continuous.

questions.question:
Read the passage and choose the correct option for the blank.

*Rahul ____ (a) cricket since he was six. Last year he ____ (b) selected for the district team, and next month he ____ (c) in the state trials.*

Blank (b):
option_feedback: There is no earlier past action here.
Correct!
*Last year* is a finished time.
*Last year* needs the past.

questions.question:
Read the passage and choose the correct option for the blank.

*Rahul ____ (a) cricket since he was six. Last year he ____ (b) selected for the district team, and next month he ____ (c) in the state trials.*

Blank (c):
option_feedback: Correct!
*next month* is in the future.
*next month* is in the future.
*next month* is in the future.

questions.question:
Read the passage and choose the correct option for the blank.

*The Taj Mahal ____ (a) by Shah Jahan in memory of his wife. Every year millions of tourists ____ (b) it. Recently, the government ____ (c) new rules to protect the marble from pollution.*

Blank (a):
questions.explanation: A past action done to the subject → *was built*.
option_feedback: The building happened in the past (the 17th century).
The Taj Mahal did not build anything; we need the passive *was built*.
The Taj Mahal is the thing built; the passive is needed.

questions.question:
Read the passage and choose the correct option for the blank.

*The Taj Mahal ____ (a) by Shah Jahan in memory of his wife. Every year millions of tourists ____ (b) it. Recently, the government ____ (c) new rules to protect the marble from pollution.*

Blank (b):
option_feedback: *Every year* shows a repeated present habit.
Tourists do the visiting: active voice.
Correct!
*tourists* is plural: no -s.

questions.question:
Read the passage and choose the correct option for the blank.

*The Taj Mahal ____ (a) by Shah Jahan in memory of his wife. Every year millions of tourists ____ (b) it. Recently, the government ____ (c) new rules to protect the marble from pollution.*

Blank (c):
option_feedback: *Recently* refers to a completed action.
Correct!
*Recently* with a result that matters now is best in the present perfect.
There is no second past action.

questions.question:
Read the passage and choose the correct option for the blank.

*When I ____ (a) the station, the train ____ (b) already. I ____ (c) for the next one for two hours before it finally arrived.*

Blank (a):
questions.explanation: Later of two past actions → simple past.
option_feedback: Correct!
The reaching is the later action; the leaving of the train came first.
The story is in the past.
Reaching a place is a short completed action.

questions.question:
Read the passage and choose the correct option for the blank.

*When I ____ (a) the station, the train ____ (b) already. I ____ (c) for the next one for two hours before it finally arrived.*

Blank (b):
option_feedback: *already* shows the train went before I reached: past perfect.
The story is in the past.
*already* shows the leaving was complete.
Correct!

questions.question:
Read the passage and choose the correct option for the blank.

*When I ____ (a) the station, the train ____ (b) already. I ____ (c) for the next one for two hours before it finally arrived.*

Blank (c):
questions.explanation: Duration before another past action → *had been waiting*.
option_feedback: The story is in the past.
The duration before *arrived* is best shown by the past perfect continuous.
Correct!
*for two hours before it finally arrived* shows duration up to a past moment.

questions.question: Identify the error and choose the correct correction: *He did not went to school yesterday.*
questions.explanation: *did* + V1: *He did not go to school yesterday.*
option_feedback: *did not* is correct.
Correct!
*yesterday* needs the past *did*; the problem is the V2 after it.

questions.question: Identify the error and choose the correct correction: *She have been working here for ten years.*
questions.explanation: *She* takes *has*: *She has been working here for ten years.*
option_feedback: Correct!
*has been working* is the correct present perfect continuous.
*ten years* is a length of time: *for* is correct.
*been* + V-ing is correct here.

questions.question: Identify the error and choose the correct correction: *I am living in Surat since 2015.*
option_feedback: *2015* is a point of time: *since* is correct.
*in Surat* is correct for a city.
*am live* is not a correct form.

questions.question: Identify the error and choose the correct correction: *The museum remain closed on Mondays.*
option_feedback: We say *on Mondays*.
*on Mondays* (every Monday) needs no apostrophe.
Correct!
*remains closed* is correct.

questions.question: Identify the error and choose the correct correction: *We have visited Agra last summer.*
questions.explanation: A finished time (*last summer*) → simple past.
option_feedback: *visit* takes no *to*.
Correct!
*last summer* is correct.
*have visit* is not a correct form.

questions.question: Identify the error and choose the correct correction: *When I reached the cinema, the film already started.*
option_feedback: Correct!
Reaching happened later; it stays in the simple past.
*When* is fine for a short action.
*the film* is correct.

questions.question: Identify the error and choose the correct correction: *I will tell her when she will come.*
option_feedback: The main clause can keep *will*.
*when* is right for a single event.
*tell her* is correct.

questions.question: Identify the error and choose the correct correction: *The teacher said that the sun rose in the east.*
option_feedback: *rises in the east* is the standard phrase.
*in the east* is correct.
Correct!
*said* is fine; the truth stays present.

questions.question: Identify the error and choose the correct correction: *I am knowing the answer to this question.*
option_feedback: *this question* is correct.
Correct!
*the answer* is correct.
*the answer to a question* is correct.

questions.question: Identify the error and choose the correct correction: *She has wrote three poems for the school magazine.*

*She* takes *has*.
*for the school magazine* is correct.

questions.question: Identify the error and choose the correct correction: *While we were playing, it begin to rain.*

option_feedback: Correct!
*we* takes *were*.
*While* is right for the longer action.
*began to rain* is correct.

questions.question: Identify the error and choose the correct correction: *He said that he will meet me the next day.*
option_feedback: With *the next day* the report is clearly in the past.
*the next day* is acceptable.
*meet me* is correct.

questions.question: Identify the error and choose the correct correction: *Look! The children plays in the garden.*
option_feedback: The meaning needs the plural.

*Look!* is an imperative.

questions.question: Identify the error and choose the correct correction: *Did you saw the comet last night?*
option_feedback: *last night* is correct.
Correct!
*last night* needs *Did*.
*the comet* is fine for a known comet.

questions.question: Identify the error and choose the correct correction: *Mohan has gone to Delhi a week ago.*
option_feedback: Correct!
*gone to Delhi* is correct.
*a week ago* is correct.

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.

option_feedback: *were* is past.
